A refutation-grade defect would be booked outside that set regardless of the contract, per the batch18 elf-b18-002 precedent (VF-01, major on a false verification claim). This audit considered booking VF-02 at major on exact parity with that precedent and DECLINED, with the reasoning stated in that finding's 'why': batch18's false claim was a universal quantifier over the shipped bank that was the sole stated ground for its conclusion, whereas VF-02 is a false descriptor of four visible words whose design conclusion is independently established three separate ways (M-TELL's 1.00 token ratio, the blind G-STEM null on q5, and the bank norm showing rhyme-uniformity is not a lane invariant). cold_solve.method: Solved from the final passage alone before reading any rationale or gate verdict. Every one of the twenty options was written into its completed frame in full and argued FOR, then defeated on a named ground, before the key was recorded.
cold_solve.result: 5 of 5 MATCHING the shipped key string C B A D C. No gap admitted a second grammatically-and-idiomatically defensible option.

per_gap.insertions: 'to take the long outlook' — no reading in English; a long-term outlook is HELD, never TAKEN in this frame. 'to take the long gaze' — a long gaze is good English as a noun phrase, but a gaze is held, met or returned; the light-verb 'take' does not select it. 'to take the long sight' — long sight and long-sighted are both real BrE (hyperopia), which gives the shape an ear-fit, but the collocation does not exist and the ophthalmic sense is wrong here anyway. 'to take the long view' — the fixed idiom.
per_gap.external: 'take the long view' is a dictionary HEADWORD in Merriam-Webster, Cambridge, Longman (LDOCE), Collins, Wiktionary and The Free Dictionary, glossed as evaluating by long-term rather than immediate results — exactly the sense the paragraph has already earned with 'twelve years from a key'. Uniquely fixed on 'view'.

per_gap.insertions: 'Increasingly, a plot cannot be inherited' — parses, and is the sharpest lure for a reader primed by a twelve-year wait; defeated twice over. The passage dates nothing and reports no change in how the clause is applied (the generator's carried ground), AND paragraph 4 runs the other way: the succession the clause forbids SUCCEEDS there (the nephew ends with the tenancy in his name and the transfer gets one flat line), so a reading on which the prohibition is progressively tightening is contradicted by the passage's own closing movement, not merely unsupported by it. That is a stronger defeat than the rationale claims. 'Curiously' — asserts the rule is odd; closed in as many words by the repaired next sentence, 'nobody disputes it or finds it odd'. 'Privately' — inverts paragraph 1 ('Nothing here is hidden: the order is numbered'), and the adverb dangles, having no subject whose privacy it could predicate. 'Strictly' — locks.
per_gap.external: The key is DICTIONARY-ATTESTED in the frame, not merely discourse-selected: Collins gives 'strictly' a distinct adverb sense, 'precisely or candidly; factually, as in the phrase strictly speaking', and OED/Oxford Learner's carry the same sense. Bare sentence-initial 'Strictly,' is the ordinary BrE ellipsis of 'strictly speaking'. The repair's 'as written' names the letter-of-the-rule reading that this sense encodes, so the key is now selected positively.

per_gap.insertions: 'waiting for dead men’s coats' — the thematically strongest of the three, since a coat is the classic inherited garment and the passage is about inheritance; forms no idiom of waiting. 'waiting for dead men’s gloves' — 'the gloves are off' and 'handle with kid gloves' put gloves in the register of set phrases and all the digging in the passage gives them an occasion; neither yields this frame. 'waiting for dead men’s hats' — the REPAIR UNDER TEST; forms no idiom at all and can only be read literally (see external). 'waiting for dead men’s shoes' — the proverb.
per_gap.external: REPAIR VERIFIED SOUND IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. (i) 'dead men's shoes' / 'waiting for dead men's shoes' is dictionary-attested in Collins, Wiktionary, The Free Dictionary, Green's Dictionary of Slang, wordhistories.net, phrases.org.uk and Proverb Hunter, all glossing it as advancement obtainable only when the post-holder dies or retires — which is precisely the mechanism the paragraph has built ('Movement comes when somebody else stops'). No source records a 'boots' variant. (ii) An exact-quoted search for 'dead men's hats' / 'dead man's hats' returns NO idiom: the hits are the shoes proverb itself, an NPR piece on the decline of men's hats, and a one-off blog title about a Mad Men episode. Hats has no succession, waiting, inheritance or death idiom. (iii) The withdrawn option is independently vindicated as a real defect: beyond 'step into a dead man's shoes', 'fill someone's boots' and 'die with one's boots on', there exists a published novel titled DEAD MEN'S BOOTS (Mike Carey, 2007, Felix Castor #3) — a literal instance of the string in the frame, which the round-1 G-DISTRACTOR flag did not even cite. Withdrawing 'boots' was correct, not cosmetic.

per_gap.insertions: 'not approving, but it is not gracious either' — the designed trap and the only real contender; defeated by the CONJUNCTION, which is the clean discriminator. A same-side second term takes 'and' ('he wasn't kind, and he wasn't gracious either'); 'but' demands an opposite pole ('he wasn't rude, but he wasn't friendly either'). With 'gracious' the 'but' has no contrast to carry. Context confirms: a committee that has just put the tenancy in the nephew's name has accommodated him, so 'not gracious' misdescribes the act the minute records. 'cautious' — wrong axis (care, not approval), and a committee giving a transfer exactly one line is being careful, so the word is doubly wrong. 'anxious' — wrong axis (worry), and the committee is recording an outcome it has already allowed. 'censorious' — the pole 'approving' opens.
per_gap.external: n/a — decided by construction, not by collocation. Note that this gap is engineered against the pick-the-moderate heuristic: the key is the severe word and both cautious-sounding options are wrong.

per_gap.insertions: 'The rule has not been summoned' — real semantic pull (summoning is a calling-upon and committees do summon), but the object of 'summon' is a person or a meeting, never one's own regulation. 'The rule has not been provoked' — direction reversed: a rule provokes a reaction, it is not itself provoked. 'The rule has not been evoked' — the strongest lure, one letter from the key and shared Latin root, but 'evoke' takes a memory, an image or a feeling, and a clause in a handbook is none of those. 'The rule has not been invoked' — the standard verb for a rule that stands on the books and has not been applied.
per_gap.external: 'invoke a rule / a clause' is the standard collocation. Internally the frame is coherent: one name at the top since 2019, three plots offered, three refusals, and a rule that fires on the SECOND refusal — so the rule was available twice and was not used, which is exactly what 'has not been invoked' says.

Worse for the note: G-REGISTER states the concentration is 'three of this unit's five gaps are idiom collocations AGAINST b18-002's MIXED BUDGET' — but elf-b18-002's own gap_type_map is {1 collocation, 2 polarity, 3 collocation, 4 connective, 5 collocation}, i.e. three collocation gaps, identical to this unit's. The substantive question — whether the ELF cloze lane systematically over-weights fixed-phrase RECALL relative to inference, since every unit in the bank is 3/5 collocation — is real and belongs at BLUEPRINT level, which is where batch18's audit also placed it. Bare sentence-initial 'Strictly,' is the ordinary BrE ellipsis of 'strictly speaking', so the gap is NOT purely discourse-selected: the key has lexical licensing of its own, and 'Increasingly / Curiously / Privately' have no such sense available in this frame. findings.claim: generator_meta.toponym_note describes the unit's own shipped text and is FALSE IN TWO PARTICULARS. The sentence reads: 'the setting is carried entirely by common nouns (the site, the trading hut, the committee, the gate) and by numbers (118 plots, 61 names, 2019)'. (a) The passage says 'Fifty-eight names are on it', not 61. (b) The word 'committee' does not occur anywhere in the passage.
findings.evidence: Checked programmatically on the final bytes. re.findall for the names figure over the passage returns ['Fifty-eight'] and nothing else; '61' does not occur in the passage; "'committee' in passage.lower()" returns False (the passage says 'the minutes give it one line' and never names the body that keeps them). The other four enumerated items DO check out: 'the site' (‘The site has a hundred and eighteen allotment plots’), 'the trading hut' (‘the trading-hut window’), 'the gate' (‘the walk from the gate’), '118 plots' and '2019'. The 61 figure is a fossil of an authoring-time edit that the NOTES record honestly at §9b: the draft opened at 'Sixty-one names', which echoed the batch19 sibling gen-elf-long's title 'Sixty-One Fires', and was changed to fifty-eight. clone_note (e) carries the CORRECT figure ('a hundred and eighteen, fifty-eight, four to seven, twelve...'), so the two metadata blocks contradict each other.
findings.why: It is a checkable, self-asserted statement about the unit's own bytes, and it is wrong. There is also a small live hazard rather than a purely cosmetic one: a repairer who trusted toponym_note over the passage and 'reconciled' the number upward to sixty-one would reintroduce the exact intra-batch title echo that §9b deliberately removed. This is NOT the batch18 VF-01 class — the load-bearing claim of toponym_note ('NO invented place name and no named institution') is independently TRUE and was verified here by enumerating every capitalised token in the passage, and the false items are illustrative parentheticals rather than the ground of any compliance conclusion.
findings.disposition: CONTENT SHIPS; METADATA TO BE CORRECTED. Change '61 names' to '58 names' and strike 'the committee' from the common-noun list (or replace it with 'the minutes', which does occur). No key, option, stem, prompt, rationale or passage byte is affected.

findings.claim: questions[5].rationale opens: 'All four options are past participles ending in -oked, so the rhyme is exact and the frame takes any of them grammatically.' The gap-5 option set is [A summoned, B provoked, C invoked, D evoked]. 'summoned' does not end in -oked and does not rhyme with the other three. The same false description is repeated in generator_meta.rule11_note ('-oked past participles') and twice in gen-elf-cloze.NOTES.md (§6 set table and Appendix A's rule-11 re-audit table).
findings.evidence: Trivially checkable on the bytes: endswith('oked') returns False for 'summoned' and True for provoked/invoked/evoked. Phonologically /ˈsʌmənd/ against /-ˈvəʊkt/ — different final consonant cluster, no rhyme. Confirmed by grep: the '-oked' descriptor occurs at questions[5].rationale, at rule11_note, and at NOTES.md lines 160 and 364.
findings.why: It is a false, self-asserted claim about the item's own design, and unlike VF-05 no charitable reading rescues it. It matters more than an ordinary typo because it sits in the RATIONALE, which is the student-facing teaching payload of an English-language coaching product, and because it is offered as the ground for the design property that shape gives no purchase. It also conceals a real, if small, asymmetry: 'summoned' is the visible form outlier in the set, so a test-wise solver applying 'the odd-shaped option is the distractor' would narrow four options to three, which would make the unit's own §8 claim that 'blind performance is at chance (1-in-4 per gap)' overstated for gap 5. THIS AUDIT CONSIDERED BOOKING IT AT MAJOR on parity with batch18's VF-01 and DECLINED, because the design conclusion survives independently in three ways that batch18's did not: (i) M-TELL passes with an option length ratio of 1.00 against a 2.36 cap; (ii) the actual blind reviewer, G-STEM r2 on q:5, looked at this exact set and returned NOT_ANSWERABLE / pick null, i.e. the theoretical narrowing did not convert; and (iii) decisively, rhyme-uniformity is NOT a lane invariant — all 70 shipped cloze option sets were enumerated and the majority are not rhyme-uniform (elf-b18-002 gap 1 price/charge/toll/cost, gap 3 ground/field/horse/floor, gap 5 cast/deal/strike/land; elf-b16-002 gap 5 gait/stride/pace/step; elf-b17-002 gap 3 word/honour/face/trust). The lane's real invariant is POS uniformity plus semantic-field uniformity, both of which this set satisfies fully; at three-quarters rhyming it is MORE form-uniform than the bank median, not less.
findings.disposition: CONTENT SHIPS; RATIONALE AND METADATA TO BE CORRECTED before the unit is shown to a student. The cheap and correct fix is to fix the description, not the option: 'All four options are past participles, three of them rhyming exactly on -oked' — applied to questions[5].rationale, to rule11_note's set gloss, and to the two NOTES tables. Do NOT swap 'summoned' out: it is the semantically best-earned distractor in the set (summoning is genuinely a calling-upon and committees genuinely summon; what they summon is a person or a meeting, never their own rule), and replacing it would cost more discrimination than the rhyme buys.
findings.key_impact: none — key C ('invoked') is correct and singly defensible, confirmed by this audit's cold solve and by both G-KEY r2 votes on the final bytes

findings.claim: The kept surname 'Thrusselby' sits at Levenshtein distance 2 from 'Thrussell', a real and attested English surname — and the generator's own originality_note NAMES Thrussell as real ('a real surname, per Geneanet, SurnameDB and forebears.io'). The same originality_note then rejects a different candidate on exactly this ground: 'Grimshall was REJECTED anyway and never used, because it sits two letters from the very common real surname Grimshaw and the batch17 addendum bars near-duplicates.' The distance-2 relation between the KEPT name and a real surname the log itself cites was never computed, never named and never dispositioned — by the generator, by G-REGISTER (which screened Thrusselby only against the bank's '-by' cluster), or by any other gate.
findings.evidence: Levenshtein computed here: Thrusselby–Thrussell = 2; Thrusselby–Thursby = 4 (Thursby is both a Cumbrian village and a real surname, surfaced by this audit's fiction-residue leg and not previously named anywhere in the chain); Thrusselby–Thrussington = 6; Thrusselby–Thrupp = 6. Against the bank the nearest '-by' name is Ludderby at 6, which reproduces G-REGISTER's declared figure exactly, and every other listed '-by' surname is 7–8. en.wikipedia exact phrase "Thrussell" returns totalhits=63 with a notable bearer (David Thrussell).
findings.why: This is an evidence-chain gap rather than a demonstrated collision. On the merits the name looks clean: 'Thrusselby' has zero bearers and zero places on four independent indexes, the full pair returns zero everywhere, and the two-character difference is an ADDITIVE Danelaw place-suffix (-by) rather than a tail substitution, so it reads as a different name-formation and not as a misspelling of Thrussell — which is materially unlike Grimshall/Grimshaw, where the substitution reads as a typo of a very common name, and where commonness was part of the generator's stated ground. But a refute-directed audit should not supply that reasoning silently on the generator's behalf: the generator applied a two-letter rule to a candidate it rejected and did not apply it to the candidate it kept, and no gate caught the asymmetry.
findings.disposition: RECORD AND DISPOSITION EXPLICITLY. This audit's recommendation is KEEP: the name is unborne on every index probed, the -by formation is a legitimate and distinct construction, and Thrussell is rare rather than 'very common'. But the disposition should be written into the originality_note (or the assembly record) rather than left implicit, and 'Thrussell' and 'Thursby' should join the recorded neighbour list so a future generator does not coin a third name into the same corner. Owner-level override remains available: the batch16 'Skarpbo' precedent shows real-neighbour calls can be reversed after ship.

findings.claim: questions[4].rationale says the sentence 'reports a committee that has watched a plot pass to a nephew IN THE TEETH OF ITS OWN CLAUSE'. The passage says the opposite, in its own words: 'The clause cannot reach what grows around it.'
findings.evidence: The clause the passage states is 'a plot cannot be inherited' and 'The tenancy ends when the tenant does'. The paragraph-4 transfer is inter vivos: 'A tenant in her eighties takes on a nephew as a helper... When the tenancy is put in his name'. The tenant is alive; nothing is inherited; the clause is not breached. That is precisely the passage's argument — the practice routes AROUND the rule rather than defying it, which is what the paragraph's opening sentence announces and what the whole written-rule-against-grown-practice arc turns on.
findings.why: The rationale asserts a defiance the passage explicitly denies, and in doing so it flattens the unit's best idea. This is teaching payload: a student reading it is told the committee tolerated a violation, when the point is subtler and better — that the clause never engaged. It is also mildly self-undermining, since the same rationale relies on the committee's even-handedness to license 'not approving, but not censorious either'.
findings.disposition: CORRECT THE RATIONALE. 'in the teeth of its own clause' → something like 'in a way its own clause cannot reach'. Six words; no key, option or passage byte affected.
findings.key_impact: none — the minute is neutral on either reading, so key D stands

findings.claim: questions[4].rationale says the four options are '-ous adjectives of manner and attitude, FULLY SUFFIX-RHYMED'. gracious /ˈɡreɪʃəs/, cautious /ˈkɔːʃəs/ and anxious /ˈæŋ(k)ʃəs/ share /-ʃəs/; censorious /sɛnˈsɔːriəs/ ends /-ɔːriəs/ and rhymes with glorious, not with the other three. It is also the only four-syllable option and the longest by two characters.
findings.evidence: Character lengths in set 4: gracious 8, cautious 8, anxious 7, censorious 10. Syllable counts 2/2/2/4. Phonological endings /-ʃəs/ × 3 against /-ɔːriəs/.
findings.why: Booked at note rather than minor because a charitable ORTHOGRAPHIC reading of 'suffix-rhymed' — 'they share the written -ous suffix' — is true, which is not available for VF-02's '-oked' claim. It is recorded because the sentence is offered as the ground for 'neither shape nor collocation separates the set', and on this gap the marked member is the KEY, which is the direction that would reward a 'pick the unusual word' heuristic. Two independent things cap it: M-TELL passes at a 1.00 option length ratio, and the blind G-STEM r2 reviewer looked at this exact set, explicitly noted that 'censorious is a corpus-frequency outlier', reasoned that 'rare words are as often traps as keys', and returned NOT_ANSWERABLE / pick null. The asymmetry did not convert.
findings.disposition: Soften the wording when VF-02 is repaired — 'all four take the -ous ending' rather than 'fully suffix-rhymed'. No content change.

findings.stage_challenged: register / evidence chain (G-REGISTER round-2 byline sweep)
findings.claim: verdicts-gregister-r2.jsonl states: 'A byline sweep over all 21 shipped ELF units confirms the bare form is the bank's dominant one (14 of 21)'. Recount gives 13 of 21, and the word 'shipped' is doing loose work — there are 65 shipped ELF units in candidates-final, and the 21 the gate means is the en-dash-era cohort, which includes batch18 and batch19, neither of which is promoted.
findings.evidence: Enumerated mechanically. The en-dash byline cohort is batch14–17 (13 units) plus batch18 (4) plus batch19 (4) = 21, which reproduces the gate's denominator. Bare within it: elf-b14-001, b14-002, b14-003, b15-003, b15-004, b16-004, b17-001, b17-004, b18-001, b18-004, b19-001, b19-002, b19-004 = 13. Credentialled: b15-002, b16-002, b16-003, b17-002, b17-003, b18-002, b18-003, b19-003 = 8. Over the FULL shipped ELF bank the direction inverts: of 65 units, 43 carry a byline and only about 13 of those are strictly bare, so credentialled is the bank's dominant form roughly 2:1.
findings.why: The gate used the sweep to support DISCHARGING a binding batch18 disposition, so the arithmetic is part of the evidence chain and should be right. The direction of the claim is nonetheless correct under the intended cohort reading (13 of 21 is still a majority), and — decisively — the discharge does not depend on it at all: the batch18 disposition named 'bare byline' as an accepted remedy in as many words, and the unit adopted it. Everything else in the same verdict checks out exactly: the three quoted predecessor bylines (elf-b16-002 Kester Orrenshaw, elf-b17-002 Georgina Chalkwright, elf-b18-002 Prudence Dabbershaw) are verbatim; the ELF-long lane (b14-001, b17-001, b18-001) is bare in all three; the TYPE-002 lane (b15-004 through b18-004) is bare in all four; and 'three of batch19's four ELF units now carry a bare byline and elf-b19-003 is the sole credentialled one' is true.
findings.disposition: DISCHARGE STANDS. Correct '14 of 21' to '13 of 21' and qualify 'shipped' to 'en-dash-era' if the verdict is ever re-issued. No action owed by the unit.

findings.stage_challenged: carried note: idiom-recall concentration (aggregated by this audit)
findings.claim: The carried minor — 'three of this unit's five gaps are idiom collocations against b18-002's mixed budget' — is REFUTED as a unit-level concern, and its stated comparison is false.
findings.evidence: All twelve cloze units carrying a gap_type_map (eleven shipped plus batch18) were enumerated: every one has exactly THREE collocation gaps out of five. Ten are the literal 3 collocation / 1 polarity / 1 connective triple; elf-b10-002 labels one gap 'sense/collocation' and elf-b9-002 labels one 'collocation/polarity-mirror' and carries 2 polarity. Restricting to the exact literal triple over the eleven shipped units gives nine, reproducing batch18's VF-11 figure exactly. Critically, elf-b18-002 — the unit the gate names as the 'mixed budget' contrast — has gap_type_map {1 collocation, 2 polarity, 3 collocation, 4 connective, 5 collocation}: three collocation gaps, identical to this unit's.
findings.why: The concern was framed as a deviation from a sibling, and the sibling has the same budget. Left uncorrected, a phantom concern gets carried forward and repaired against, which is worse than either shipping it or fixing it at the right level.
findings.disposition: NOT A UNIT DEFECT; do not carry forward against this unit. The real question — whether an ELF cloze lane in which every single shipped unit devotes 3 of 5 gaps to fixed-phrase recall is testing too much memory and too little inference — is genuine and belongs to the BLUEPRINT, exactly where batch18's audit placed it. Recommend it be raised there rather than at any unit's V-FINAL.

findings.stage_challenged: blind marked-member surface, cross-gap (aggregated by this audit)
findings.claim: Two of the five sets contain a member that is marked on surface form, and in one of them it is the key. Set 4: 'censorious' is the only four-syllable option, the longest by two characters, the only one not rhyming on /-ʃəs/, and by a distance the rarest — and it IS the key. Set 5: 'summoned' is the only option not on the -oked rhyme — and it is a distractor. Set 2 has a milder version: the key 'Strictly' is the shortest of the four adverbs.
findings.evidence: Character lengths per set — gap 1 outlook 7 / gaze 4 / view 4 / sight 5 (key tied shortest); gap 2 Increasingly 12 / Strictly 8 / Curiously 9 / Privately 9 (key shortest); gap 3 shoes 5 / coats 5 / gloves 6 / hats 4 (key tied); gap 4 gracious 8 / cautious 8 / anxious 7 / censorious 10 (key longest); gap 5 summoned 8 / provoked 8 / invoked 7 / evoked 6 (key middle, inside the rhyming trio).
findings.why: This is the batch18 VF-07 concern re-tested on a different unit, and it comes out weaker here because the directions CANCEL: at gap 4 'pick the marked member' finds the key, at gap 5 it eliminates a distractor, and at gaps 1 and 3 it returns nothing. No single blind rule wins more than chance across the sheet, and the two extremes point opposite ways, so a solver cannot calibrate one from the other. The empirical check agrees: the blind G-STEM r2 reviewer returned NOT_ANSWERABLE / pick null on all five gaps, and explicitly reasoned about and rejected the censorious rarity signal.
findings.disposition: Within tolerance; recorded so the running surface pattern stays visible across the lane. No repair owed. M-TELL passes at a 1.00 option length ratio, which is the mechanical guard that actually gates this.

findings.claim: connective_ordinal_note declares ordinal 2 'the value rolled for this unit from the permitted set {2,3,5}' with the prior uses batch18=4, batch17=1, batch16=4, batch15=5. All four prior figures are EXACT. But within the permitted set, 2 is the most-saturated choice available and 5 the least.
findings.evidence: Connective-gap ordinals across all thirteen shipped cloze units plus batch18, read from gap_type_map: ordinal 1 × 1 (b17), ordinal 2 × 3 (b10, b12, b13), ordinal 3 × 5 (b3, b4, b8, b9, b11), ordinal 4 × 2 (b16, b18), ordinal 5 × 1 (b15). Choosing 2 makes it four uses across fourteen units; choosing 5 would have made it two.
findings.why: No rule is breached — the addendum imposes no least-used requirement, only that the ordinal vary and that recently-used values be avoided, and the most recent ordinal-2 use is batch13, six batches back. The generator's declaration is honest and its arithmetic is right. Recorded only so the saturation stays visible to whoever sets the next roll.
findings.disposition: Info. Suggest the next cloze brief prefer ordinal 5 or 1 to level the distribution.

findings.claim: The published wait reconciles, but sits in the low half of its own stated band. 58 names on the list and 'four to seven plots come free in an ordinary year' bracket the bottom of the list at 8.3 to 14.5 years; the passage states 'twelve years from a key', which implies about 4.8 plots a year.
findings.evidence: 58/7 = 8.3, 58/4 = 14.5, 58/12 = 4.83. Twelve is comfortably inside the band. The authoring-time change recorded at NOTES §9b (sixty-one → fifty-eight, to clear the echo with the sibling title 'Sixty-One Fires') moved the implied throughput from about 5.1/yr to about 4.8/yr — both inside 'four to seven'. There is no defect; the check is recorded because a cloze passage whose arithmetic did NOT reconcile would be one, and because a future editor tempted to 'restore' sixty-one should know both what it would fix (nothing) and what it would break (the intra-batch title echo).
findings.disposition: No action. Do not change the figure.

findings.claim: typography_note says 'Spaced en dash (U+2013) only — once inside paragraph 2 and once opening the byline line'. The byline dash is line-initial, so it is spaced on one side only. Separately, the rationales mix apostrophe styles: 64 straight and 3 curly, including within a single sentence of the gap-3 rationale ('dead men’s hats' curly beside "one's hat" straight).
findings.evidence: Counted on the bytes: em dash U+2014 occurs ZERO times in the entire file, which is the load-bearing part of the note and is correct. En dash U+2013 occurs twice in the passage, at 'when somebody else stops – a knee that will not manage the walk' and at the line-initial '– Lettice Thrusselby'. The passage's own apostrophes are uniformly curly (3, zero straight) and it contains no quotation marks of any kind, both as declared.

The rationale apostrophe mixing is cosmetic and is not covered by any declared rule.
findings.disposition: No action required. If the rationales are ever normalised for rendering, normalise apostrophes with them.

resolved_findings.id: G-DISTRACTOR round-1 flag, gap 3 (option D 'boots' arguable)
resolved_findings.round_1_claim: 'boots' was flagged ARGUABLE: the allotment setting supplies a strong pull toward working footwear, and the step-into-a-dead-man's-position sense does attach to boots in modern usage, so an examinee could argue the variant is live.
resolved_findings.repair: fleet-repair-1: option D 'boots' → 'hats', staying inside the plural-worn-article family the set is built on; the gap-3 rationale was rewritten to argue 'hats' and to record the withdrawal, and rule11_note and grammar_guard_note were re-synced.
resolved_findings.verification: RESOLVED, verified on the final bytes, and the FLAG IS INDEPENDENTLY VINDICATED BY THIS AUDIT ON EVIDENCE THE GATE DID NOT HAVE. (a) The swap is present: options are [shoes, coats, gloves, hats], key still A, all four bare plural count nouns after a plural possessive, POS uniform, one token each. (b) 'hats' forms no idiom in the frame — an exact-quoted search for 'dead men's hats' / 'dead man's hats' returns no fixed phrase at all, only the shoes proverb itself plus an NPR feature on the decline of men's hats and a one-off blog title about a Mad Men episode; the real hat idioms (at the drop of a hat, old hat, hats off to, wear several hats, pass the hat, talk through one's hat, eat one's hat) concern suddenness, staleness, congratulation, multiple roles, collecting money, nonsense and self-abasement, and none concerns succession, waiting, inheritance or death. (c) The withdrawn option was genuinely defensible, and MORE so than the round-1 gate argued: besides the live idioms 'step into a dead man's shoes', 'fill someone's boots' and 'die with one's boots on', there exists a published novel titled DEAD MEN'S BOOTS (Mike Carey, 2007, Felix Castor #3) — a literal instance of the string in this exact frame, which neither the gate nor the generator cited. (d) The key is untouched and re-verified: 'waiting for dead men's shoes' is attested in Collins, Wiktionary, The Free Dictionary, Green's Dictionary of Slang, wordhistories.net, phrases.org.uk and Proverb Hunter, glossed as advancement obtainable only when the post-holder dies or retires, and no source records a 'boots' variant. (e) G-DISTRACTOR r2 returned pass on all five gaps of the repaired bytes. The one cost of the swap is recorded honestly at cleared item 6: gap 3 is now a pure proverb-recall item with three field-parallel non-idioms and no near-miss at all, which trades some discriminative texture for the removal of a defensible second answer. For a shipping item that is the right trade.

resolved_findings.round_1_claim: Unlike gaps 1, 3 and 5 this gap is not carried by collocation — 'Curiously,' and 'Increasingly,' are both idiomatic English sentence adverbs in the frame, so the key 'Strictly,' was selected only by the discourse that followed. Sound but weaker than its neighbours as an English-idiom item.
resolved_findings.repair: fleet-repair-1: the discourse anchor was strengthened by one clause on either side of the existing sentence — 'That is the clause, and nobody disputes it.' → 'That is the clause as written, and nobody disputes it or finds it odd.' The generator explicitly recorded that 'Increasingly' is still carried on the pre-existing ground and labelled that a carry, not a claim of a new anchor.
resolved_findings.verification: RESOLVED, verified on the final bytes, and STRONGER THAN THE TICKET CLAIMS. The from-span is absent and the to-span present. 'as written' names the letter-of-the-rule reading the key encodes, so the key is selected positively; 'or finds it odd' closes 'Curiously' in as many words. Beyond the ticket, this audit establishes two grounds the unit does not use: (i) the key is DICTIONARY-ATTESTED in the frame — Collins gives 'strictly' a distinct adverb sense, 'precisely or candidly; factually, as in the phrase strictly speaking', so bare sentence-initial 'Strictly,' has lexical licensing of its own and the gap is not purely discourse-selected, which answers the gate's core objection at its own level; and (ii) 'Increasingly' has a second defeater in paragraph 4, where the forbidden succession SUCCEEDS, so a reading on which the prohibition is progressively tightening is contradicted rather than merely unsupported. Gap 2 cold-solves SINGLE here, and both G-KEY r2 votes returned B on the repaired bytes citing the new anchor by name. Residual, recorded and not repaired: gap 2 is still the only gap in the unit whose key requires reading forward past the gap, which is structural to a sentence-initial connective at the head of a paragraph rather than a defect.

cleared.item: INTERNAL CONSISTENCY OF THE PASSAGE'S OWN ARGUMENT
cleared.result: Coherent, and better constructed than the rationales give it credit for. The published arithmetic reconciles (VF-12). The closing fact reconciles with the rule it names: three refusals against a rule that fires on the second means the rule was available twice and used neither time, which is exactly what 'The rule has not been invoked' says. The central move is sound and non-trivial — the clause forbids INHERITANCE, the nephew's transfer is INTER VIVOS, so the practice routes around the rule rather than defying it, which is precisely what 'The clause cannot reach what grows around it' announces. The unit's declared non-tidiness holds: paragraph 3's residue (the concrete path from the seventies, the plum tree planted too near the boundary, the strawberry bed under couch grass) genuinely serves no argument in paragraph 4. The passage takes no side and closes open, as the arc declares. The only crack found is at VF-04, where a rationale contradicts this reading rather than the passage contradicting itself.

ship_recommendation: SHIP-READY ON CONTENT; three metadata/rationale corrections owed first, none of which touches a key, an option, a stem, a prompt or a passage byte. audit_note: REFUTATION ATTEMPTED AND FAILED AGAINST THE ITEM. Every avenue the brief opened was pursued: a cold solve of all five gaps with all twenty options written into their frames and argued for before being put down; claim-by-claim verification of all five rationales, with external dictionary attestation obtained for every idiom any key depends on; span-by-span verification of the four fleet-repair-1 tickets against the shipping bytes; an independent law-16 re-run with the generator's own two positive controls and its null control plus four adversarial extras of my own; an independent re-run of all six mechanical gates and re-derivation of every band figure with mech.py's own tokenizer; and programmatic re-derivation of every falsifiable generator_meta claim against the 114-unit shipped bank plus batch18. THE ITEM IS SOUND. The key string is CBADC and I reproduce it 5 for 5 with no second defensible option at any gap. BOTH REPAIRS UNDER TEST HOLD, and both are stronger than their tickets claim. Gap 3: 'hats' forms no idiom in the frame on an exact-quoted check, while the withdrawn 'boots' turns out to be MORE defensible than the round-1 gate argued — beyond 'step into a dead man's shoes' and 'die with one's boots on' there is a published novel literally titled 'Dead Men's Boots' (Mike Carey, 2007) — so the withdrawal was a real fix and not a cosmetic one. Gap 2: the anchor repair is present verbatim, and the gate's core objection (that the key was discourse-selected rather than collocation-locked) is answered at its own level by something the unit never claims — Collins carries 'strictly' as a distinct adverb sense meaning 'precisely or candidly; factually, as in the phrase strictly speaking', so bare sentence-initial 'Strictly,' has lexical licensing of its own; and 'Increasingly' has a second defeater in paragraph 4, where the forbidden succession actually succeeds. WHERE REFUTATION SUCCEEDED IS THE METADATA AND THE TEACHING PAYLOAD, and three findings there are worth stating plainly. VF-02: the gap-5 rationale tells the student that all four options 'end in -oked, so the rhyme is exact', and 'summoned' does neither; the claim is repeated in rule11_note and twice in the NOTES. VF-04: the gap-4 rationale says the plot passed to the nephew 'in the teeth of its own clause', when the passage's own sentence is 'The clause cannot reach what grows around it' — the transfer is inter vivos and the clause never engaged, which is the unit's best idea and the rationale flattens it. VF-01: toponym_note describes the unit's own bytes and gets two of six particulars wrong, saying '61 names' where the passage says fifty-eight and listing 'the committee' among the setting's common nouns when that word appears nowhere in the passage. I CONSIDERED BOOKING VF-02 AT MAJOR on exact parity with batch18's VF-01 — a checkably false claim offered as verification — and declined for a reason I want on the record so adjudication can overrule it: batch18's false claim was a universal quantifier over the shipped bank and was the sole stated ground for its conclusion, whereas this one is a false descriptor of four visible words whose conclusion survives three independent checks, the third of which is decisive — I enumerated all 70 shipped cloze option sets and rhyme-uniformity is NOT a lane invariant (elf-b18-002 alone ships price/charge/toll/cost, ground/field/horse/floor and cast/deal/strike/land), so at three-quarters rhyming this set is more form-uniform than the bank median, not less, and the psychometric consequence I had started to construct collapses. CARRIED NOTES WEIGHED. The idiom-recall concentration note is REFUTED as a unit-level defect on stronger evidence than batch18 had: all twelve cloze units carrying a gap_type_map devote exactly three of five gaps to collocation, so this unit is the invariant rather than an outlier — and the comparison the gate actually drew is false, since elf-b18-002, named as the 'mixed budget' contrast, is itself 3 collocation / 1 polarity / 1 connective. The concern is real one level up, at the blueprint, and should be raised there. The gap-2 weakness is resolved, with the residual being structural rather than repairable: it is the only gap whose key requires reading forward past it, which is what a sentence-initial connective at the head of a paragraph is. ONE ITEM I COULD NOT DISMISS AND DID NOT TRY TO. VF-03: 'Thrusselby' sits two edits from 'Thrussell', a real surname the generator's own log names as real, and the same log rejects a different coinage precisely for sitting two letters from a real surname. On the evidence the name is clean — zero bearers and zero places across four indexes, with the -by suffix making it a distinct Danelaw formation rather than a misspelling — but the check was never run on the name that was kept, and that asymmetry belongs in front of adjudication rather than behind an auditor's judgement.
